issues.legal_issue: A vacancy-notification order that is a preliminary step to a final allotment may be challenged in a proceeding against the final allotment even if it was not challenged independently when made.
material_facts: The rent authority declared the building vacant and later allotted parts of it to occupants.
The landlord challenged the allotment orders in revision, arguing that no vacancy existed and that the prescribed procedure had not been followed.
The reviewing court set aside the allotments, but the High Court reversed solely because the vacancy notification had not been challenged earlier.
The governing scheme contained no provision making the vacancy notification final or barring a later challenge to it.
issues.conclusion: The vacancy notification could be challenged in the revision against the final allotment. The High Court erred in treating the failure to challenge it earlier as a bar, so its judgment was set aside and the matter remanded for fresh consideration, including the propriety of the vacancy notification and the effect of a later cancellation of one allotment.
issues.legal_principle: An interlocutory order that is a step toward a final order may generally be challenged when the final order is challenged, unless a statutory provision makes the interlocutory order final or precludes that challenge. The Court relied on Moheshur Singh v. The Bengal Government and Sheonath v. Ramnath, and applied Section 105(1) and Order XLIII Rule 1A of the Code of Civil Procedure, while noting the exceptions in Sections 97 and 105(2). It also relied on Satyadhan Ghosal v. Smt. Deorajin Debi and Amar Chand Butail v. Union of India. Ganpat Roy v. Additional District Magistrate did not hold that failure to challenge a vacancy notification immediately forfeited the right to challenge it in a revision against allotment; it recognized that the notification could also be challenged independently. The contrary view in the High Court decision under appeal and Smt. Kunj Lata v. Xth Additional District Judge was overruled.

predicates.rent_control_allotment_challenge: A party is challenging a final allotment in a proceeding under a rent-control scheme.
predicates.vacancy_order_precedes_final_allotment: The challenged vacancy determination was a preliminary step leading to the final allotment.
predicates.no_law_bars_later_challenge: No applicable rule makes the preliminary vacancy determination final or bars its challenge in the proceeding against the final allotment.

issues.definition: When a rent-control allotment challenge concerns a final allotment preceded by a vacancy determination, and no applicable rule bars a later challenge, the vacancy determination may be challenged with the final allotment.

issues.legal_issue: A landlord who acquires the property during pending proceedings may enforce the landlord's rights in respect of the property.
material_facts: The original owner sold the building while the allottees' High Court proceeding was pending.
The purchaser pursued the appeal as the assignee landlord.
issues.conclusion: The assignee landlord was entitled to enforce rights in respect of the property, including on the assumption that the occupants were tenants under the assignee.
issues.legal_principle: Section 109 of the Transfer of Property Act permits an assignee of the landlord's interest to enforce the landlord's rights in respect of the property.

predicates.landlord_rights_dispute: A proceeding concerns the enforcement of a landlord's rights in respect of a property.
predicates.property_transferred_to_assignee_landlor: The property was transferred to a person who acquired the landlord's interest.

issues.definition: When a landlord-rights dispute concerns property transferred to an assignee landlord, that assignee may enforce the landlord's rights.

issues.legal_issue: Occupants who have not paid rent or occupation charges during prolonged litigation may be required to make provisional payments as a condition of continuing to contest the proceedings.
material_facts: The occupants had remained in possession for many years during the litigation.

The Court found that they had not paid rent from the beginning, although they claimed to have tendered sums calculated using assessed annual values and said those tenders had been returned undelivered.
The landlord sought payment of arrears and ongoing charges while the proceedings remained pending.
issues.conclusion: The occupants were directed to make provisional payments of arrears and ongoing monthly charges, with the payments subject to adjustment in the rent-recovery decree. An occupant who did not comply was not entitled to contest the pending proceedings or be heard.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that allowing occupants to contest prolonged proceedings without paying arrears and continuing occupation charges would be a travesty of justice. It ordered provisional payments as a condition of participation, with adjustment to be made consistently with the decree in the separate rent-recovery action.

predicates.pending_rent_proceeding: A proceeding concerning the occupant's right to remain in the premises is pending.
predicates.occupant_remains_in_possession: The occupant continues to occupy the premises while the proceeding is pending.
predicates.prolonged_nonpayment: The occupant has failed to pay rent or occupation charges over a prolonged period during the litigation.

issues.definition: When a rent proceeding is pending, the occupant remains in possession, and nonpayment has continued for a prolonged period, provisional occupation payments are required to continue contesting the proceeding.

issues.legal_issue: For a period after an occupant ceases to be entitled to possess the premises as a tenant, the landlord's entitlement is measured by mesne profits rather than being capped at standard rent.
material_facts: The occupants continued to hold the premises while entitlement to possession was disputed.
No rent rate appeared to have been fixed for the premises, and the occupants did not appear to have sought its fixation.
The Court stated that the landlord's entitlement would be measured from the date on which the occupants were found to have ceased to be entitled to retain possession as tenants.
issues.conclusion: For any period after the occupants were found to have ceased to be entitled to possession as tenants, they would be liable for rent equivalent to mesne profits, and the landlord's entitlement for that period could not be pegged to standard rent.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on Atma Ram Properties (P) Ltd. v. Federal Motors (P) Ltd. for the principle that, after a tenant ceases to be entitled to retain possession, the landlord may claim mesne profits rather than an amount limited to standard rent.

predicates.rent_control_possession_dispute: A proceeding concerns an occupant's continuing right to possess premises as a tenant under a rent-control arrangement.
predicates.occupant_ceases_to_be_entitled_as_tenant: The occupant is found to have ceased to be entitled to retain possession in the capacity of a tenant.

issues.definition: In a rent-control possession dispute, once an occupant is found to have ceased to be entitled to possession as a tenant, the landlord is entitled to an amount equivalent to mesne profits.
